changes.description: Initial snapshot: the subcommand→capability-requirement table as committed when the drift guard landed. Breaks nothing — this records the live contract as-is; motivated by #2386 (TBH-1) silently narrowing backlog-dedupe/gather-issue-context/gather-pr-context requirements and breaking every shipped config.

Require exact separately brokered issue-read capabilities for built-in commands so issue-write grants cannot release GOOBERS_CRED_GITHUB_ISSUES_READ; existing workflows that need issue reads must declare the explicit read capability.

Add pr-comment-watch: label open goober PRs carrying unaddressed human comments (github:issues:write via label-issue). Purely additive — a new command with one requirement; no existing command's requirements change, so every shipped config keeps compiling.

Add file-issues (#2251, TBH-1 first slice): the nomination workflows' deterministic issue filer. --check requires the exact github:issues:read grant for the dedupe scan; the write path requires github:issues:write. The filer never applies goobers:approved (the SEC-047 trust label is a maintainer's decision), so it declares no github:issues:approve requirement. Purely additive — a new command; no existing command's requirements change, so every shipped config keeps compiling.

file-issues (#2251, decision 004): declare github:issues:approve as an OPTIONAL use. The filer applies goobers:approved only to a nomination whose evidence matches a deterministic tool finding (go vet / golangci-lint / go test) byte for byte, and only when the autoApprove=deterministic-only INPUT opts in — the manifest sees only args, so it cannot require the credential on that input; admission requires it through the policy table instead (the input prescribes approve-issue, whose contract requires github:issues:approve). The label add goes through the approve credential alone. Optional is never required, so no shipped config's admission changes.

Add ResultFileSupport (#4415): a tri-state (Unsupported/Always/Optional) classification of whether a built-in command produces a result file, resolved via the new SupportsResultFile accessor and consumed by a new admission check (v_2_0/v_3_0 compile.go's resultFileContractProblem) that rejects a stage declaring inputs.resultFile/expectedOutputs for a command that never writes one (e.g. record-merge-refusal). Purely additive metadata: an explicit ResultFileOptional override on reconcile-branches/telemetry-query (previously implicit Unsupported by omission, since they declare no ResultFile string, even though both can write one conditionally). Deliberately NOT extended to the capability-free built-ins builtincmd also inventories (__demo-provider, cancel-pending-ci, check-fail-first, docs-churn, gate-removal-guard, ios-simulator-test, mcp-io, self-update, validate) — this manifest covers only commands with declared capability requirements (see the package comment), and SupportsResultFile's ok=false for an absent command is treated as permissive by the new check, not as ResultFileUnsupported, so leaving them out changes nothing about what it rejects. No existing command's Capabilities/ResultFile/claim-ledger fields change, so every shipped config's capability admission is unaffected.

Add preflight-repo-write (#4414): the repository-write credential preflight stage, wired first in the implementation workflow. Requires repo:push, the same capability push-branch already requires — the check runs read-only requests with that credential. Purely additive — a new command with one requirement; no existing command's requirements change, so every shipped config keeps compiling.

Add security-alerts-query (#2984, #2987): the read-only security-alert intake connector stage. Each of the two feeds requires its own EXACT least-privilege read grant, selected by --source: github:code-scanning:read for code scanning, github:dependabot-alerts:read for Dependabot. Exact, so an issue-write or PR-write grant can never release either credential; and split, so a workflow that only nominates dependency work never receives code-scanning access. The stage declares no write capability at all — it reads alerts and emits an artifact, and the nomination that follows is a separate, separately credentialed stage. Purely additive: a new command with new capabilities; no existing command's requirements change, so every shipped config keeps compiling.

Add recovery-resume and recovery-restore (#4494) to workflow admission, requiring repo:push to fetch the configured current main when restoring retained implementation in a stage. Both are newly inventoried workflow commands; no previously inventoried command capability, result-file or claim-mutation contract changes. Standalone operator recovery-restore retains its configured authentication path. Existing configurations retain their admission behavior.
